scene_report.narration_text: In March 2024, Kendrick Lamar ignited a massive controversy by rejecting the idea of a rap 'Big Three' alongside Drake and J. Cole.
His message was simple: there is only one king.
Drake fired back with the track 'Push Ups', mocking Kendrick's career and reputation.
Kendrick responded by unleashing 'Euphoria', a brutal six-minute diss track attacking his rival.
The conflict turned deeply personal when Drake released 'Family Matters', making explosive allegations about Kendrick's private life.
Less than an hour later, Kendrick shocked everyone with 'Meet the Grahams', firing back with disturbing allegations about Drake's family.
On May 4, Kendrick dropped 'Not Like Us', a devastating track accusing Drake of serious misconduct.
While Drake denied these claims, the song exploded, becoming a global anthem that won five Grammy Awards.
What started as a battle for the throne became one of hip-hop's most unforgettable rivalries.
